question:
(a) Explain why free electrons in a metallic conductor do not produce current in the absence of an electric field.
(b) What happens when a potential difference is applied across the conductor?
(c) State the direction of conventional current in relation to electron motion.

options.A:
(a) Without an electric field, electron thermal motions are random and average velocity is zero, so there is no net charge flow.
(b) An applied potential difference establishes an electric field and electrons acquire drift velocity opposite to it, producing current.
(c) Conventional current is opposite to electron motion.
options.B:
(a) Electrons do not produce current because they are absent in metals.
(b) Applying potential difference stops the electrons.
(c) Conventional current is in the same direction as electron motion.
options.C:
(a) Random electron motion produces a steady current.
(b) Applying potential difference creates positive electrons.
(c) Conventional current has no direction.
options.D:
(a) Electron velocities add in the same direction even without field.
(b) Applying potential difference makes electrons drift in the direction of the field.
(c) Conventional current is perpendicular to electron motion.
